subject: Staircase commit proposal — exit & renewal mechanics
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Morris <claire.morris@helixtx.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Staircase commit proposal — exit & renewal mechanics

Claire — great to meet last week. Per our conversation, attached is a concise staircase (annualized) commit option that Helix can elect for a 3-year engagement. High-level highlights: 
- Year 1: 40% of committed spend as prepay with 10% term discount
- Year 2: 30% prepay with step-down discount (7%)
- Year 3: 30% prepay with 5% discount; optional renewal window at year-end

Key asks we want to confirm early: whether Helix expects co-terming across internal business units, and whether accounting prefers a single upfront invoice or staggered billing per year. I attached an "Redwood_Staircase_Option.xlsx" with amortization examples and per-token unit economics.

Also flagged two contract points to avoid future friction: reasonable early-exit refund formula (amortize consumed vs unconsumed) and a renewal crediting approach that avoids double-counting usage for true-ups. Draft amendment (v1) included in attachment; legal suggested we capture an escrow-style amortization table.

Suggested next step: 30-min call with procurement + legal to run through the refund math and get mutual agreement on the amortization basis and rounding rules. Proposed times: Thu 8/20 10:00am PT or Fri 8/21 9:00am PT.

Thanks — let me know which works and I can get a calendar invite out.

Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: Redwood_Staircase_Option.xlsx (spreadsheet — amortization by month; sample invoices)

From: Claire Morris <claire.morris@helixtx.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@helixtx.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 08:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Staircase commit proposal — exit & renewal mechanics

Ben — thanks for the doc. Quick answers up front: Helix prefers a single invoice per year (stated for internal audit) but we can accept staggered invoicing by agreement. Co-terming: we will likely want a single co-term across three product teams — I need to confirm whether that is strictly required. 

Key redlines from procurement/legal we will need before signing: 
- Hard cap on early termination liability limited to unconsumed prepaid amount less a 5% administrative fee; no clawbacks beyond that.
- If Redwood proposes escrow-style amortization, Helix needs month-by-month visibility and a right to audit usage credits during the year.
- Renewal credits: Helix will not accept credits that reduce committed spend for renewal calculations; credits should apply to short-term true-ups only.

Also, our tax team prefers refunds (if any) to be processed as credit notes rather than cash refunds.

Let's take the call Fri 8/21 9:00am PT — that works for procurement and legal on our side.

Claire Morris
Head of Procurement | Helix Therapeutics
claire.morris@helixtx.com | +1 (617) 555-0189

Attachment: none

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Morris <claire.morris@helixtx.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 09:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Staircase commit proposal — exit & renewal mechanics

Claire / team — appreciate the clear redlines. To be transparent, internal legal flagged two negotiation levers we can flex to bridge to Helix's asks: 
1) Amortization transparency: we can provide a monthly amortization dashboard (read-only link) and include audit windows (once per year) for usage reconciliation.
2) Early termination math: we prefer a pro-rata amortization with a 10% administrative processing fee OR an escrow-style arrangement where Helix holds prioritized credits that run down monthly; in the escrow case Redwood would accept a lower administrative fee (5%), but would require a commitment that renewal/expansion conversations cannot retroactively reduce previously-credited committed amounts.

Proposed compromise in the attached "Draft_Amendment_v2.docx": 
- Early exit refund = unconsumed prepay balance less 7.5% admin (midpoint) OR escrow amortization at month-end with Helix audit rights. 
- Renewal crediting: credits are available only for usage true-ups within the active term year and cannot reduce the committed baseline used to calculate future term discounts.
- Co-terming: if Helix requests cross-product co-terming, Redwood will create a consolidated invoice and apply discounts to the aggregate committed amount; co-terming requires a 12-month minimum enrollment for any newly added product.

We can go over the amendment on the call. Agenda: 1) walk through refund math examples (5–10 mins), 2) choose amortization approach (10 mins), 3) confirm invoicing cadence and co-term rules (5 mins), 4) next steps for signatures.

Ben — can you invite engineering finance (Karthik) to attend the call for the amortization modeling?

Thanks — Monica
Director, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai

Attachments: Draft_Amendment_v2.docx

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Morris <claire.morris@helixtx.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2026 16:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Staircase commit proposal — exit & renewal mechanics

Claire / team — thanks for taking the call today (notes below). This thread consolidates the final numeric positions we agreed on and the model assumptions I used in the spreadsheet.

Meeting notes (summary):
- Chosen path: escrow-style amortization with monthly drawdown; Helix will see a read-only monthly dashboard.
- Early exit refund formula: remaining unconsumed prepaid balance less a 6% administrative fee (compromise between 5% and 7.5%). Refunds issued as credit notes applied within 30 days.
- Renewal mechanics: credits from true-ups apply to the invoice for the same contract year only and do not reduce the committed baseline for subsequent term discount calculations.
- Co-terming: Helix accepted consolidated co-term for the three product teams; any product added mid-term inherits prorated enrollment and does not reset the aggregate discount tier.

Attached I exported the final amortization tab from the workbook and highlighted the cells used to calculate the 6% admin fee. Link to the dashboard will be provisioned after signature.

Next steps: Ben to send amendment (v3) with the 6% admin fee language and DocuSign link; Claire to confirm internal approval and sign.

Karthik Iyer
Manager, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Quoted from meeting chat: "We can make the escrow table auditable — one audit window per year should be sufficient to preserve accounting controls."
